validity.recommendation: Verify LengthKnown (684 km) and Capacity (4.0 bcm/y) against a primary planning/regulatory document rather than the wiki infobox. No independent source found states exactly 684 km for a Tieshangang(Beihai)-to-Liuzhou trunk. Independent sources instead give 1,318 km for the full Beihai-LNG external-transmission network reaching 10 Guangxi + 2 Guangdong cities (ljzfin.com, citing construction start July 2013 / trial ops March 2016 -- consistent with GEM's StartYear1=2013), and a separately-reported 731-735 km figure for a narrower Beihai-Qinzhou-Nanning corridor (found via search but I could not pin an exact, independently loadable URL for that figure, so I have NOT cited it). Before trusting 684 km as settled, also confirm P4721's route doesn't double-count mileage already carried on P4715 (Beihai-Maoming Branch, 207 km, a different/eastward branch toward Guangdong) or P4718/P4719 (both explicitly 'Liuzhou Transmission Station'-originating branches, i.e. likely sequential continuations FROM the point where P4721 terminates, not overlapping with it) -- my read of the topology is that P4721 is probably the distinct long-haul trunk and NOT a duplicate of those branches, but the length figure itself is not independently pinned down.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence: solidly confirmed independent of GEM/wiki. The operating company is real and verifiable: cnstock.com (2024-06-13, verified) profiles '国家管网广西公司' (National Pipeline Network Guangxi Company) under the headline 'from one pipe to one network,' consistent with the wiki's own claim that the pipeline transferred to PipeChina in July 2020. ljzfin.com (verified, tokens '1318' and '2013' both present) independently confirms a Beihai LNG terminal external-transmission pipeline exists, gives construction start July 2013 (matches GEM StartYear1=2013) and trial operation March 2016, a design diameter of 800mm, and states the network totals 1,318 km across 18 stations/49 valve chambers reaching major Southwest China cities -- this is a materially different (much larger) total than GEM's 684 km, though it likely describes a broader distribution scope (trunk + downstream city branches) rather than one discrete segment, so it's a caveat rather than proof GEM is wrong. Classification (Fuel=Gas, a gas transmission trunk) is correct -- this is unambiguously the gas trunk delivering regasified LNG from the Beihai terminal, not a gathering/feeder line. Duplicate check against the roster: P4715/P4716/P4718/P4719/P4720/P4723 all share the identical pipeline_name 'Guangxi LNG Terminal Transport Pipeline' and are described on the SAME gem.wiki page as named sub-branches (Beihai-Maoming Branch=P4715 207km/3.3bcm/y match exact; Liuzhou-Guilin Branch=P4719 155.7km/2.5bcm/y match exact; Liuzhou Branch~27km=P4718 29km close match; a further 'Qinzhou-Fangchenggang' 70.44km branch mentioned on the page has no obvious matching PID in the 43-row roster and may be untracked). Given P4718 and P4719 both explicitly originate FROM 'Liuzhou Transmission Station' -- the same district/prefecture where P4721 (684km) TERMINATES -- the most likely topology is P4721 = the long-haul trunk arriving at Liuzhou, with P4718/P4719 as further downstream spurs from that arrival point, not parallel duplicates of the trunk's mileage. I therefore did NOT flag this as concern_type=duplicate, but a human should still eyeball the two pipelines' route geometry (once routed) to rule out overlap, especially given the unresolved 1,318km discrepancy above. Owner/Operator: Owner1 'Guangxi Natural Gas Pipeline Co Ltd' (100%) matches the QCCOwner Chinese name '广西天然气管道有限责任公司' and is consistent with independent sourcing; however a Baidu Baike lookup (NOT cited/used as a source per project standards -- crowd-sourced, unverifiable tier) surfaced an unconfirmed claim that this company's equity changed on 2025-08-11 to give PipeChina 100% direct control (implying it may not have been 100% PipeChina-owned before that date) -- this is an attribution lead worth someone chasing through an actual PipeChina/SASAC disclosure filing, not something I'm willing to act on from a wiki-tier source alone.

fills.researcher_notes: ljzfin.com states construction of the Beihai LNG external-transmission pipeline commenced July 2013, matching GEM's StartYear1=2013 (single strong source; only supports Year1, not the 2015/2019 phase dates, which remain unsourced).

cnstock.com profiles the operating company as '广西天然气管道有限责任公司' (Guangxi NATURAL GAS Pipeline Co. Ltd.), confirming this is a gas transmission pipeline (commodity=Gas), consistent with its role delivering regasified LNG from the Beihai terminal.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched for anything newer than the sheet's 2025-08-25 LastUpdated that would contradict 'operating' -- found none; instead found corroborating evidence the underlying operator/network is actively managed and expanding through 2025 (e.g. 国家管网集团广西公司 reported handling a different Guangxi products pipeline's throughput in Aug 2025, and NEA's March 2025 national pipeline-operations meeting references ongoing Guangxi-region gas infrastructure work), consistent with a mature, still-operating trunk. Direct dated evidence specific to this pipeline is the cnstock.com 2024-06-13 profile of the Guangxi pipeline company (post-PipeChina-transfer operations). No evidence of any status change, outage, or decommissioning found in English or Chinese search. Single directly-on-topic source only (medium tier) -- a stronger, more current confirmation would strengthen this.

summary: P4721 (Guangxi LNG Terminal Transport Pipeline, Tieshangang->Liuzhou, 684km/4.0bcm/y, operating) is a real, correctly-classified gas trunk (operator/company independently verified); status=operating confirmed (medium tier, 2024-06 evidence). Flagged a spec concern: no independent source pins the exact 684km/4.0bcm/y figures -- one verified source instead gives 1,318km for the broader Beihai-LNG distribution network -- though after checking topology against sibling rows (P4715/P4718/P4719) I don't believe this is a duplicate/double-count; recommend a primary-document length check.
